title: Priority-based Usage Credits, Billing Failover & Audit Acceptance
creator: Priya Kapoor
summary: Define and deliver a deterministic policy and acceptance criteria for prioritizing usage credits across plans, implementing a billing failover path when metering or billing pipelines are delayed, and ensuring invoice/audit traceability for all emergency credit operations.
background: Customers have inconsistent behavior when account-level credits, plan-level priority credits, and temporary emergency credits interact across multiple routes and models. Recent incidents showed delayed billing pipelines causing customers to be charged incorrectly when usage ingestion lagged; engineers applied manual credits without consistent audit trails. We need a repeatable product definition that codifies priority rules, an automated failover mode for billing, and explicit acceptance criteria to satisfy finance and compliance audits.
problem_statement: Ambiguity in credit precedence and lack of automated billing failover leads to incorrect invoices, noisy manual interventions, and missing auditability. Goal is to eliminate manual edge-case credits, reduce invoice corrections, and provide deterministic outcomes for customers under ingestion/processing delays.
goals: Define a precedence order for credit application (entitlement -> plan credits -> emergency credits -> overage billing)
Implement a billing failover mode that defers invoicing but preserves usage ordering and customer-visible balances when ingestion or billing pipeline errors occur
Create an auditable trail for any automated or manual credit adjustments with reasons, actor, and rollback metadata
Ship acceptance tests and dashboards that verify correct credit application in 10 representative scenarios (including bursts, dual-plan memberships, and deduplicated route replays)
non_goals: Redesigning pricing tiers or changing per-token pricing in this ticket
Building a full dispute automation workflow (we will provide hooks for downstream workflows but not the dispute resolution UI)
detailed_requirements: Credit precedence: system MUST apply credits in this order: plan-specific allocations -> per-caller credits -> reserved burst buckets -> emergency ad-hoc credits -> then invoice overage charges.
Per-route tagging: every incoming usage record must carry route_id, plan_id, caller_id, and ingestion_timestamp to support deterministic join semantics in billing aggregation.
Atomic application: credit application logic must be atomic per-usage event (either usage consumes a credit or increments overage counter), with idempotency guaranteed for at-least-once ingestion.

Billing failover mode: when ingestion or billing processing latency exceeds defined SLOs (see monitoring), system should switch to failover mode that: a) preserves raw usage events in cold storage, b) prevents invoicing for affected window, c) surfaces affected accounts in Finance queue.

Emergency credit API: expose an authenticated endpoint for ops to apply time-bound credits with reason enum (incident, goodwill, trial-extension) and mandatory memo field; all ops actions must create an immutable audit record.

Invoice reconciliation: reconciler job must flag any mid-cycle credit edits and produce a pre-invoice delta that Finance can review; automatic corrections must be restricted to defined thresholds (<$200 or <2% of invoice) else require manual approval.
UI/Console indicators: Console must show a per-account 'credit precedence map' and a banner when failover mode is active for that region/account.
Test harness: create 10 canonical scenarios (described in attachments) with expected finalized invoice lines for automated acceptance tests.
Security: emergency credit endpoints require MFA enforcement and a jumbo audit retention (7 years) for accounts in regulated regions.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Unit and integration tests cover all 10 canonical scenarios and pass in CI; expected invoice line items match golden files for each scenario.

AC-2: Simulated billing pipeline delay >30 minutes triggers failover mode; affected accounts are marked and invoices are withheld for that window. Post-replay reconciliation yields identical invoice amounts as the non-failover baseline within allowed tolerance.
AC-3: Emergency credit creation produces an immutable audit record (actor, timestamp, reason, original_balance, new_balance, correlation_id) surfaced in Console and available via audit logs API.
AC-4: Automatic reconciler respects correction thresholds; any automatic correction outside thresholds creates a Finance review task and is blocked from auto-apply.
AC-5: E2E load test with concurrent usage from 5k callers consuming credits validates atomicity and idempotency (no double-consumption) under at-least-once ingestion semantics.

AC-6: Manual ops runbook tested: applying and rolling back an emergency credit within a sandbox account produces consistent audit entries and reversible invoice adjustments in the staging invoicing system.
AC-7: Compliance verification: security team validates MFA gating on emergency credit endpoint and signs off on retention policy before release.
engineering_notes: Prefer implementing precedence logic in billing aggregation layer to keep runtime path read-only; proto-change may be required for routed usage events.
Add canonical ids to usage events at the ingestion boundary to avoid downstream joins relying on eventually consistent metadata.
Failover mode to be coordinate with regional routing logic; plan for feature flag per-region to ramp behavior incrementally.
Estimate ~6 sprint-days of work for core engine changes + 2 sprint-days for Console indicators and runbook documentation (estimate surface only).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): implement precedence logic, emergency credit API, and unit tests. Enable in staging for 2 weeks and run the 10 canonical acceptance tests.
Phase 2 (canary): enable in 5% of accounts in a non-regulated region with Console banner and Finance monitoring enabled for 2 weeks.
Phase 3 (regional ramp): expand to all accounts in region after Finance signoff; enable MFA enforcement for emergency credit endpoint.
Phase 4 (global): enable retention policy and longer-term cold storage hooks for audited records; retire temporary debug flags.
Rollback: global feature flag to revert precedence behavior if invoice divergence > threshold during ramp.
monitoring_and_metrics: Count of emergency credits applied per day by reason enum
Number of accounts in failover mode and average duration per incident
Invoice correction rate (post-finalized invoices) and number of manual credit interventions per 1000 accounts
Reconciliation delta distribution (per-account) after replay vs baseline
Audit log ingestion success and retention compliance alerts
